nodes.name: Schedule - Daily
nodes.notes: 07:00 - an hour after the KPI refresh, so the day's KPIs are already rebuilt. FX 05:00 -> KPI 06:00 -> detection 07:00.

nodes.name: Manual Run
nodes.notes: On-demand run for backfills, demos and CLI execution. Same path as the schedule.

parameters.query:
-- Open the run ledger entry before the detector is called.
--
-- ingestion_runs is shared by every scheduled pipeline; source says which.
-- A crash after this point leaves a visible 'running' row rather than silence.
--
-- The window is the span of KPI dates the detector will consider, so the ledger
-- answers "which dates did this run account for?" without reading anomaly_daily.
WITH span AS (
    SELECT min(calendar_date) AS from_date, max(calendar_date) AS to_date
    FROM salesops.kpi_daily
)
INSERT INTO salesops.ingestion_runs
    (batch_id, source, window_from, window_to, status, n8n_execution_id)
SELECT
    gen_random_uuid(),
    'anomaly-detector',
    COALESCE((SELECT from_date FROM span), CURRENT_DATE),
    COALESCE((SELECT to_date   FROM span), CURRENT_DATE),
    'running',
    $1
RETURNING
    batch_id::text    AS batch_id,
    window_from::text AS window_from,
    window_to::text   AS window_to,
    run_id;

nodes.name: Run Detection
nodes.notes: Service-name DNS, never localhost. Full recomputation: baselines look backwards, so new KPI data changes earlier verdicts. 3 attempts, 5s apart; the service returns 503 on failure so a failed run is never mistaken for a run that found nothing.

nodes.name: Validate Detection Result
nodes.notes: Shape check. Throws if results were dropped or the payload is malformed.

nodes.name: Finalize Detection Run

parameters.query:
-- Close the run.
--
-- Success is derived from what the detector actually processed, never from the
-- workflow having reached this node. A run that evaluated nothing is not a
-- success, and a run that hit KPI rows it could not score is only a partial one.
--
-- Count semantics, chosen to satisfy the ingestion_runs balance CHECK
-- (received = accepted + rejected + duplicate):
--
--   received  = KPI dates evaluated
--   accepted  = results written (scored or explicitly unscored - every date
--               evaluated gets a row, so nothing is silently dropped)
--   rejected  = dates whose KPI row lacked FX coverage. A real data gap, and
--               the only condition that makes this run 'partial'.
--   duplicate = 0. Results are upserted in place, so a re-run overwrites rather
--               than duplicating; there is no "already present" category.
--
-- Dates skipped for insufficient history are NOT rejections. Early in a series
-- there is genuinely nothing to compare against; that is a correct outcome, and
-- treating it as a fault would leave every run permanently 'partial' and train
-- the reader to ignore the status.
UPDATE salesops.ingestion_runs r
SET finished_at       = now(),
    records_received  = $2::int,
    records_accepted  = $3::int,
    records_rejected  = $4::int,
    records_duplicate = 0,
    status            = CASE
        WHEN $2::int = 0 THEN 'partial'
        WHEN $4::int > 0 THEN 'partial'
        ELSE 'success'
    END,
    error_message     = NULL
WHERE r.batch_id = $1::uuid
RETURNING
    run_id,
    batch_id::text AS batch_id,
    status,
    records_received  AS dates_evaluated,
    records_accepted  AS results_written,
    records_rejected  AS dates_incomplete_kpi,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.anomaly_daily
      WHERE detector_version = $5 AND is_anomaly)::int         AS anomalies_flagged,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.anomaly_daily
      WHERE detector_version = $5 AND baseline_status = 'scored')::int AS dates_scored,
    (SELECT round(max(anomaly_score), 2) FROM salesops.anomaly_daily
      WHERE detector_version = $5)                             AS highest_score,
    round(extract(epoch FROM (finished_at - started_at))::numeric, 2) AS duration_seconds;

nodes.notes: Derives success vs partial from what was actually processed.
